verses.1: And the kings wrote concerning him, 'Righteous, righteous,' for in righteousness He makes kings to reign, those who do His will.
verses.2: And He illumines their dwelling with a light that cannot be interpreted, where Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob dwell, and David, and Solomon, and Hezekiah, and all the good kings whose dwelling is light, because they did the will of God; and not as a fortress on earth, but a fortress in heaven, excellent, surpassing, and pure, a fabric of gold and silver and jacinth.
verses.3: It is beyond the understanding of man; its appearance is bright, exceedingly a fortress of the kingdom of heaven, shining with topaz and emerald, and with darkness and splendor.
verses.4: And with every precious stone that is beyond the understanding of man, a fortress of the kingdom, bright and surpassing, which He made for Himself as a canopy, as He tells of the fortress of the kingdom of heaven; and pure is its fabric of gold and silver and jacinth, and crystal and sapphire and a fabric of jacinth and pearls.
verses.5: And likewise it is beautiful and splendid, surpassing and pure and bright.
verses.6: And it is established in righteousness and in truth, and built in tranquility and in mercy.
verses.7: And there is in it one who causes the water of life to flow, exceedingly pure like the sun, and a spring of light, and crowned with the cedars of Hermon.
verses.8: And around His house are planted the fruits of paradise, sweet ones, whose appearance and fragrance are lovely; and vines, and wine, and oil, and balsam, and good and sweet honey, the fragrance of its fruit.
verses.9: And when one enters into it, the flesh, from tasting the fragrance of its fruit, the soul goes out from the abundance of the joy that is upon it.
verses.10: And there the good kings rejoice, those who did the will of God; their food and their standing place are known; it leads to the abode of life forever in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.11: And He showed that as it is in heaven, so it is on earth; according to the greatness of their kingdom on earth, and according as men honor them and bow down to them, so also in heaven they are honored and exalted and rejoice, if they did good during their life upon the earth.
verses.12: But those who grew proud in their kingdom and in their dominion which God gave them, and did not judge with righteousness and truth, and did not deliver the oppressed and the wronged and the orphans from death, because they despised the word of the poor and the needy,
verses.13: and did not deliver the poor and the needy from the hand of him who oppressed them, and did not feed the hungry from their food, and did not give drink to the thirsty from their drink, and did not incline their ear to the cry of the orphans of the living—
verses.14: for those very ones He will bring them down into the dwelling of Sheol, the region of darkness; and according to the greatness of their glory, so their destruction and their ruin shall be multiplied. When they were at ease, that great day came which God made, and His wrath. As David says in the psalm, 'O Lord, in Your wrath do not rebuke me, and in Your anger do not chasten me.'
verses.15: And as for those who keep Your law, whether kings and rulers, or the rulers of the world, they are faithful upon the earth.
verses.16: And in heaven there is One who holds all, and all souls are in His hand, and all life is in His mouth, who gives glory to those who glorify Him, and loves those who love Him; for He reigns over all and rules all.
verses.17: And He searches the heart and the reins, for He is the King of heaven and earth, who gives his prayer to him who prays to Him with a pure heart.
verses.18: And He brings low the pride of the arrogant, who oppress the mighty and the orphans of the dead.
verses.19: It was not by your own strength that you attained this kingdom, and it was not by your own power that you sat upon this throne; but He Himself, willing it, seated you upon the throne of the kingdom. He will test you, whether you are able to rule His people, as Saul in those days, who led His people astray and was deaf to the word of God and to the word of Samuel the prophet, and did not kill the king of Amalek and his people.
verses.20: For God said to Samuel the prophet, 'Go, say to Saul: Go and strike the land of Amalek, and kill all their kings and their inhabitants, from man to beast; for they have provoked Me with transgression of the law and with the worship of gods, and bowing down to idols, and with their abominations, and with every impure deed in which there is no profit.'
verses.21: And because of this, when they provoked God, He sent word that they should be killed.
verses.22: But he spared their king, and many cattle also, and women and maidens, and gave them as a portion to the warriors. And because of this God said to Samuel the prophet, 'Because he has transgressed My word and has not obeyed My command, go, strip him of his kingdom.'
verses.23: And He anointed David the son of Jesse, that he might reign in his stead over Israel.
verses.24: But as for the other, an evil spirit entered into him, which choked him.
verses.25: For 'I gave you the kingdom, that you might do My will; and when you did great things, doing My will, I exalted you from purity. But as for you, go, say and tell him: Is this how you requite God, who made you king over His people Israel, and seated you upon the throne of His kingdom?'
verses.26: But you did not know the measure of this, that He gave you great glory and greatness.
verses.27: And Samuel the prophet went to Saul the king, and entered to him while he was standing in the plain, and Agag the king of Amalek in his pomp.
verses.28: And he said to him, 'Why have you been deaf, deaf to God who commanded you to destroy man and beast?'
verses.29: And then he was afraid, and the king rose from his throne and seized the garment of Samuel; and Samuel turned away greatly, and the garment of Samuel was torn.
verses.30: And Samuel said to Saul, 'God has torn away your kingdom.'
verses.31: And again Saul said to Samuel, 'Honor me before the people, and pray for me before God, that He may have mercy on me.' And Samuel greatly refused his word, because he feared the word of God his Creator, and did not fear the king who was about to die.
verses.32: And because of this he struck Agag the king of Amalek while food was still in his mouth.
verses.33: And as for that sinner who transgressed the word of God, an evil spirit seized him and struck his head; for God is not ashamed before a king who commits iniquity, for He is the King of kings, who commands all.
verses.34: And as for Him, there is none who can command Him, for He is the Lord of all creation, who brings low all the authority of kings and rulers who do not fear Him.
verses.35: And from Saul also the kingdom departed from him and from his son, as it is said: the house of David shall go on increasing, and the house of Saul shall go on diminishing.
verses.36: And God blotted out the seed of the house of Saul because he provoked Him, and He did not spare his allies who provoked Him with the evil of their deeds; for he who is not an adversary of the adversaries of God is himself an adversary of God.
verses.37: And he who does not reprove a sinner, when he is able to reprove him, and has the authority himself, he also is truly an adversary of God; he who does not keep the law of God has nothing.
